items.title: Awesome Rust
items.content_text:
### Applications / Utilities

*   [zerx-lab/FluxDown (⭐1k)](https://github.com/zerx-lab/FluxDown) - A multi-protocol download manager with a Rust/Tokio engine, supporting HTTP/FTP, BitTorrent, eD2K, HLS and DASH, with IDM-style dynamic segmentation, browser extensions and an aria2-compatible JSON-RPC endpoint.

### Libraries / Parsing

*   [ophi-dev/antlr-rust-runtime (⭐10)](https://github.com/ophi-dev/antlr-rust-runtime) \[[antlr-rust-runtime](https://crates.io/crates/antlr-rust-runtime)] - ANTLR v4 runtime with a pure-Rust parser generator: generates parsers directly from `.g4` grammars (no Java required), validated against the official ANTLR conformance testsuite. [![build badge](https://github.com/ophi-dev/antlr-rust-runtime/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/ophi-dev/antlr-rust-runtime/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

items.title: Awesome Go
items.content_text:
### Databases Implemented in Go

*   [MemHop (⭐6)](https://github.com/qyiun666/MemHop) - Embedded cognitive memory database for AI agents. Six-layer architecture (L0-L5), Dream consolidation pipeline, three-channel RRF retrieval (BM25 + f16 vector + entity), single .meh file, pure Go, zero infrastructure.

### Security

*   [secretgenerator (⭐9)](https://github.com/rafaelperoco/secretgenerator) - CSPRNG-backed credential generator with a versioned JSON schema for passwords, passphrases, secrets, API keys, and PINs.

items.title: Awesome Bitcoin
items.content_text:
### Utilities

*   [Freedom Clock](https://freedomclock.io) - Bitcoin-aware FIRE calculator with sell, borrow, and borrow-then-sell spend models. Converts savings and BTC holdings into years of financial freedom. Fully local, no account, MIT. Also an open-source e-ink desk device (\~$30).

items.title: Awesome Machine Learning
items.content_text:
### Python / General-Purpose Machine Learning

*   [Leanpass (⭐4)](https://github.com/Terminay/LeanPass) - A lightweight, NumPy-only autodiff library for small ML projects and learning how backpropagation works. It is 700x times lighter than Pytorch and 900x times lighter than TensorFlow.
